title: Three-month opera plan and staff roles cribsheet (v0-1)
content:
---
Document type: working draft (cribsheet)
Purpose: Rapidly align exec + team leads on the next 90-day execution rhythm, candidate OKRs, and a light staffing/roles matrix to use when communicating at the all-hands.

Context and constraints:
- This is a pragmatic, skinny plan to be reviewed in the Exec Sync (Wed 2/19) and used as the basis for the all-hands slides and the company Q1->Q2 transition notes.
- Not a final commit: we expect edits from Product, Eng, and Sales leads; this doc captures current hypotheses and open decisions.

Topline proposed narrative for the all-hands (30s elevator):
- Reinforce mission: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.
- Progress: shipped Dedicated autoscaling beta; hosted API latency P50 improved 18%; private deployment pilots started with two finance customers.
- Focus for next 90 days: (1) cost/perf optimizations (Optimize toolkit launch), (2) enterprise readiness (Private/Governance), (3) scale engineering (observability + rollout automation).

90-day strategic pillars (narrowed):
1) Production economics: reduce per-token cost for P50 workloads by 15% via batching, caching, quantization profiles.
2) Enterprise trust: complete Private onboarding checklist + SOC2 gap remediation for dedicated customers.
3) Developer velocity: Ship Console UX revisions + rollout APIs to enable canary + A/B for model rollouts.
4) Reliability runway: raise SLA coverage to include Dedicated in EU region, and reduce P99 tail latency by 20% on common models.

Candidate OKRs (working; metrics are proposals):
- O1: Lower inference unit cost while preserving quality.
  - KR1: Decrease avg effective cost/token by 15% on top-5 customer workloads (RED-2412).
  - KR2: Deploy intelligent batching to 80% of traffic from customers on Dedicated.
  - KR3: Launch Optimize recommendations pilot with at least 3 customers and measure delta in monthly cost.
  Owner: Marco Liang; contributors: Serving Runtime, Optimize

- O2: Ship enterprise-ready Private product and audit posture.
  - KR1: Close all high/critical items from SOC2 readiness report (target: 0 open high items by 2025-04-30).
  - KR2: Onboard 2 paid Private customers (pilot->contract) with verified data flows.
  - KR3: Integrate KMS/HSM with Private deployment and document operational runbook.
  Owner: Priya Nair; contributors: Private Deployments, Security

- O3: Improve developer tooling and rollout safety.
  - KR1: Console rollout orchestration (canary + auto-fallback) available to 100% of teams using model routes.
  - KR2: Reduce time-to-debug incidents by 30% via trace hooks and per-route correlation IDs.
  Owner: Sofia Ortega; contributors: Console and Tooling, Developer Experience

Quick staffing & role cribsheet (who says what at the all-hands if asked):
- CEO (town opener): 3 bullets (mission, notable wins, asks)
- VP Eng (exec readout): progress against pillars + top risk (SRE lead present)
- Head of Product (hosted/dedicated/private split): product rollout plan + feature ship calendar
- Head of GTM (sales/CS): early private wins + deployment timelines and support asks
- Eng lead (serving runtime): short demo or metrics snapshot (P50/P99 charts)
- Ops/SRE: incident response & reliability commitments

All-hands run-of-show (45 min total):
- 0-5m: Welcome + micro-story (CEO)
- 5-15m: Metrics snapshot (VP Eng) — latency/cost/usage trends
- 15-25m: Product roadmap and immediate bets (Head Product)
- 25-30m: Customer spotlight (CS) — 1 slide + quick quote
- 30-35m: Feature demo: Optimize recommendations (Product/Eng)
- 35-40m: Vision & culture micro-ask (People Ops)
- 40-45m: Live Q&A (moderated; collect questions beforehand + Slack)

Pre-reads and slide allocation (owner / slide count):
- Exec one-pager (CEO + VP Eng) — 1 slide
- Top-5 metrics: latency/cost/adoption — Eng metric owner (2 slides)
- OKR headline + key risks (Product/Eng/CS) — 1 slide
- Customer proof points (CS) — 1 slide
- Ask & how to help (People Ops + GTM) — 1 slide

Communications checklist (timeline):
- 2/18: Finalize slides for exec review (owners send to aisha@redwood.ai)
- 2/19: Exec dry run (30m; content freeze after run)
- 2/20 morning: All-hands comms emailed + Slack announcement
- 2/20 lunch: All-hands live
- 2/21: Post-mortem notes + decisions + updated OKRs posted to Confluence

Open questions / decisions needed (prioritized):
- Q1: Do we commit to the 15% cost reduction target now? (Decide: yes/no) Impact: affects Optimize resourcing.
- Q2: Which customers to highlight for Private pilot spotlight? (CS to suggest 3 names by 2/17)
- Q3: Go/no-go on canary APIs in Console for next release (Eng to present a safety plan in exec sync)

Risks & mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Quantization regressions causing customer quality complaints.
  - Mitigation: Hold small-scale quality evals + rollback policy + canary toggles.
- Risk: SOC2 timing slips delaying Private GA.
  - Mitigation: Add external audit buffer, prioritize high-impact gaps.
- Risk: Observability gaps hide tail-latency contributors.
  - Mitigation: Instrument top model routes and add P99 dashboards before ramp.

Action items (owners + dates):
- Marco: curate top-5 workloads for cost baseline (due 2/14)
- Priya: finalize Private pilot contract checklist (due 2/20)
- Sofia: Console canary API safety plan (due 2/18)
- Aisha: compile exec slides + schedule dry run (due 2/18)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compressed — treat as a playbook not a finished document. Add comments inline or ping in #all-hands-prep. If you have a sharp disagreement with a candidate KR, flag it in the doc and propose an alternate metric.

Attachments / refs (in-doc):
- Baseline cost table (link to sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDW_COST_BASELINE
- SOC2 readiness doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SOC2-READINESS
- Customer pilot case study draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDW_PRIVATE_PILOT

---
End of cribsheet.
